clue.text: Irishman left with the logical deduction from thinking?

parts.note: Descartes: 'I think, therefore I am', so the conclusion drawn from thinking is I AM

explanation.surface: An Irishman is told, a little sarcastically, that he was left holding a conclusion he reached by thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the philosophical joke: Descartes's cogito ends in 'I am'.
explanation.definitionFit: Liam is a common Irish boy's name, the short form of William.

clue.text: Stories in which you'll find yellow parrots

indicators.note: says the second piece sits inside the word for stories

parts.note: stories in the sense of fibs are lies
or is the heraldic tincture gold, i.e. yellow

explanation.surface: Tales that feature bright yellow parrots, as in a children's book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stories' looks like the start of a hidden word, but it means fibs; yellow as OR is heraldry's gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Lories are small brightly coloured Australasian parrots, a kind of the birds named.

clue.text: Bra's grime could come from waxy substance

indicators.note: something that could come from a rearrangement signals that the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Dirt on a bra might be traced back to some waxy stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambergris is a waxy secretion of sperm whales used in perfumery, an example of a waxy material.

clue.text: After running round a calm pet may be seen on the table

definitions.text: may be seen on the table

indicators.note: a pet that has been running round is in disorder, so its letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A placid pet, having dashed about, ends up sitting on the dining table.
explanation.definitionFit: A place mat is a small protective mat set under each diner's plate, an item found on dining furniture.

clue.text: Spear used in battle is terrible

indicators.note: says the letters are to be found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A spear wielded in combat is a dreadful weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A leister is a pronged spear for catching fish, a specific type of the weapon named.

clue.text: Long-faced lot, as possibly seen in religious retreat

indicators.note: possibly means the letters could form something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Gloomy-faced people, as one might find at a monastery on retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram fodder runs from 'Long-faced' to 'as', with 'seen in' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Castel Gandolfo is the papal summer residence near Rome, a retreat for the Pope.

clue.text: This writer's repeatedly upset about a US city

indicators.note: about means going round the single letter that follows
in a down clue upset turns the letters upside down, i.e. backwards
repeatedly means the piece is written twice over

parts.note: the setter saying 'this writer is' gives I'M

explanation.surface: The setter confesses to being upset time and again over some American city.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' means read upwards, so the doubled piece is turned before 'about' wraps it round the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Miami is a large city in Florida, an example of an American city.

clue.text: Money is demanded here — a potential barrier to progress

definitions.meaning: a place where a fee is charged to pass along a road
a gate across a road literally blocks travellers until they pay

explanation.surface: A spot where cash is demanded, which could hold things up.
explanation.definitionFit: A tollgate is a barrier on a road where travellers must pay a charge before continuing.

clue.text: In new development Welsh factories will be going in a straight line

indicators.note: a new development reshapes things, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A news item: Welsh factories in a new scheme will be laid out along a straight line.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means by the most direct route, measured in a straight line, as a bird travels.

clue.text: Avoid getting key cut

parts.note: Esc is the escape key on a computer keyboard
to hew is to cut with an axe

explanation.surface: Someone avoids having a key cut at the locksmith's.
explanation.definitionFit: To eschew is a formal synonym for shun or abstain from.

clue.text: Be in a spin when engaged in tricks and puzzles

indicators.note: engaged in means held inside the word for tricks

parts.note: ruses are tricks or ploys

indicators.note: spinning round turns the word be the other way

explanation.surface: Being flustered when caught up in tricks and puzzles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be' looks like a verb in the surface, but it is just two letters to be spun round.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebuses are picture puzzles in which images or letters stand for words, a kind of puzzle.

clue.text: Put in home, a good person having everything provided

parts.note: in means at home
St, short for saint, is a good person
all means everything

explanation.surface: A good person settled at home, wanting for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To install something is to fit or set it in place, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Of great significance, this could give one heart

parts.note: read as instructions, a word shattered, i.e. jumbled, yields the word heart, so EARTH plus an anagram signal makes the clue

explanation.surface: Something momentous might well stir the emotions.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer split as two words is itself wordplay whose result is 'heart'.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth-shattering describes something momentous or having enormous consequence.

clue.text: Commercial competition — what you'd expect to span Food Week?

indicators.note: to span means to stretch across, enclosing the pieces that follow

parts.note: par is the normal or expected standard
rice is a staple food

explanation.surface: Supermarket rivalry, which is to be expected across a food promotion week.
explanation.definitionFit: Shops slashing prices to undercut each other is a battle of business rivalry.

clue.text: Two soldiers maybe, very big

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
a soldier ant is a worker of a particular caste in an ant colony

explanation.surface: A pair of soldiers, perhaps of enormous size.
explanation.definitionFit: Giant as an adjective means huge or enormous.

clue.text: Relation's friend is an easy target

parts.note: an aunt is a relation, and the possessive gives AUNT'S
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A relative's friend makes an easy mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aunt Sally is a fairground figure thrown at, so figuratively someone who is a soft target for criticism; a British idiom.

clue.text: Senior ladies adore LSD surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly means the letters turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Elderly women astonishingly fond of the hallucinogenic drug.
explanation.walkthrough: LSD here is just letters, though it also recalls old British money (pounds, shillings, pence).
explanation.definitionFit: Old dears is an affectionate British phrase for elderly women.

clue.text: Rope, see, for restraining donkey

indicators.note: restraining means holding within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or see
an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: Look, a rope to hold back the donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is a rope with a running noose for catching animals.

clue.text: Cold fish now changing within and messing about

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: within means placed inside the word for fish

parts.note: ling is a fish of the cod family

indicators.note: changing means the letters of the word now alter their order

explanation.surface: A cold fish is now transforming and acting the fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold fish' reads as one unfriendly person, but it splits into C and a fish of the cod family.
explanation.definitionFit: Clowning means acting the fool, behaving playfully or foolishly.

clue.text: Laugh, being let off after job comes to premature end

indicators.note: after means the rearranged piece follows the job
ending early means the final letter is cut

parts.note: a chore is a job

indicators.note: off means out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone laughs on being released when their job finishes early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let off' reads as being excused, but 'off' is the anagram signal on 'let'.
explanation.definitionFit: To chortle is to laugh gleefully, a synonym of chuckle.

clue.text: Pop a question — its content appears to be obscure

indicators.note: the content of the phrase is what lies inside it

explanation.surface: Popping a question whose meaning seems unclear.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaque means unclear or hard to understand, a synonym of obscure.

clue.text: Group of workers holding first of strikes, being in complete agreement

indicators.note: holding means containing the letter that follows

parts.note: a trade union is an organised group of workers

indicators.note: first of means just the opening letter of strikes

explanation.surface: A trade union holding the first strikes, all of one mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'being in complete agreement', as in 'in unison'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unison is perfect accord, everyone acting or speaking together.

clue.text: Abnormal dose for suffering actress

indicators.note: suffering means damaged or in a bad way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actress suffering from an unusual dose of medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abnormal' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'suffering' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Flora Robson was a celebrated English stage and screen performer.

clue.text: Lesson to be learnt from first half of my examination

indicators.note: the first half of a two-letter word is its first letter

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A lesson drawn from the first part of my exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A moral is the lesson a story teaches.

clue.text: Emergency operation? It is organised with flair

indicators.note: organised means arranged into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An emergency operation is run with style.
explanation.definitionFit: An airlift is transporting supplies or people by aircraft, typically in a crisis.

clue.text: Enthralled by a foreign saint, congregation develops

indicators.note: enthralled means held captive, so this piece sits inside the others

parts.note: un is French for a
a fold is a church congregation, a flock

explanation.surface: Captivated by an overseas saint, a congregation grows.
explanation.definitionFit: A story or situation that unfolds develops or is gradually revealed.

clue.text: Blokes from part of Greater Manchester who flog things?

definitions.text: Blokes from part of Greater Manchester who flog things?

parts.words: Blokes from part of Greater Manchester who flog things?
parts.note: Sale is a town in Greater Manchester, so men from Sale would be ..., a punning name for people who sell

explanation.surface: Men from a Manchester suburb who make a living selling goods.
explanation.walkthrough: Sale is a town in Greater Manchester, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Salesmen are men whose job is selling goods, flogging being slang for selling.

clue.text: Pigment seen in fancy animation

indicators.note: seen in means visible within the following words

explanation.surface: A colour that appears in elaborate cartoons.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyan is a greenish-blue colour, one of the printing primaries.
